Your notes so far

  • round 1: I want the buttons to only be 5mm thck and I want their diameter to be equal to the height of the deck, otherwise move forward with the design
  • round 2: I want the buttons flush to the surface of the volume and i don't want anthing protruding
  • round 2: owner (gap answers to the flush push-back): knob = height - 4; feet on the underside are fine. Also: I also want as few screws as possible
  • round 3: the cutout doesn't need to surround the whole dial. Have a small cutout for the encoder and the button will slide over the protruding encoder

The design

A · Shell + base plate, panel-mount encoders

Round 4: one folded shell (top + 4 walls) and one flat base plate. The encoders panel-mount in the front and right walls through small holes; the 39 x 5 caps slide onto the protruding shafts. Everything else is flush: rear sockets sit 1 mm inside the wall and plugs reach in. The plate with the Pi stack lifts in from below and takes 2 screws from underneath; the screen is taped in.

Mechanism
encoders nutted into the shell walls; plate with Pi and DAC lifts in from below; 2 screws from underneath; caps pushed on
Layout
Pi flat, USB-C side at the rear, USB/Ethernet flush behind the left wall; front encoder in front of the Pi; side encoder beside the SD end
Load path
knobs -> walls -> shell -> plate -> feet -> shelf
Process
laser-cut flat, 6 hand folds on perforated lines (UNTESTED recipe); plate is flat

Flat pattern: Shell (top + 4 walls)

6 folds by hand, 5052-H32_1.0. Untested folds: no coupon has held for this recipe yet.

Flat pattern: Base plate with encoder tabs

0 folds by hand, 5052-H32_1.0.
